text: The study was a dim, old fashioned chamber. <break time="0.8s" /> Festooned with cobwebs. <break time="0.8s" /> And sprinkled with antique dust. <break time="0.8s" /> Where tall bookcases of oak. <break time="0.8s" /> Lined the walls. <break time="0.8s" /> Over the central bookcase. <break time="0.8s" /> Stood a bronze bust of Hippocrates. <break time="0.8s" /> With which according to some authorities. <break time="0.8s" /> Doctor Heidegger was accustomed to consult. <break time="0.8s" /> In all difficult cases. <break time="0.8s" /> In the darkest corner. <break time="0.8s" /> Hung a tall, narrow mirror. <break time="0.8s" /> Within which it was fabled. <break time="0.8s" /> The spirits of all the doctors dead patients dwelt. <break time="0.8s" /> The opposite side of the room. <break time="0.8s" /> Was ornamented with the portrait. <break time="0.8s" /> Of a young lady who many years before had been on the point of marrying Doctor Heidegger. <break time="0.8s" /> But, being affected. <break time="0.8s" /> With some slight disorder. <break time="0.8s" /> She had swallowed. <break time="0.8s" /> One of her lovers prescriptions. <break time="0.8s" /> And died on the bridal evening. <break time="0.8s" /> The greatest curiosity of the study. <break time="0.8s" /> Was a ponderous book. <break time="0.8s" /> Bound in black leather. <break time="0.8s" /> Which was well known. <break time="0.8s" /> To be a book of magic. <break time="0.8s" /> On the summer afternoon of our tale. <break time="0.8s" /> A round table stood. <break time="0.8s" /> In the middle of the room. <break time="0.8s" /> And on it was placed. <break time="0.8s" /> A cut glass vase of beautiful form. <break time="0.8s" /> The sunshine came through the window. <break time="0.8s" /> And fell upon the vase. <break time="0.8s" /> So that a mild splendor. <break time="0.8s" /> Was reflected from it. <break time="0.8s" /> Onto the ashen faces. <break time="0.8s" /> Of the five old people.
